evals.prompt: Check my email for job updates.
evals.expected_behavior: Invokes the skill. First confirms a connected email tool is available (stops and says so if not, without guessing at statuses). Searches the lookback window (3 days, or 14 on first run) for ATS senders, application/interview/offer subject patterns, and company names drawn from active tracker rows. Classifies each hit per the table and writes changes only through scripts/tracker_io.py, appending a [email-sync <date>] breadcrumb. Report leads with interview requests and offers before status-update counts.

evals.prompt: It's been a rough week of waiting -- can you see if any of the jobs I applied to have moved forward, or if I've gotten any bad news?
evals.expected_behavior: Invokes the skill even without the exact trigger phrasing, since the intent is checking application-related mail against the tracker. Interview requests and rejections are classified per the table (interviewing with stage/date; rejected with date and one-line reason), recruiter outreach for new roles becomes a deduped status=new row, and anything not cleanly matching a table row is listed as ambiguous rather than force-classified.

evals.prompt: Anything interesting in my inbox today, like newsletters or stuff from my mom?
evals.expected_behavior: Does not invoke the skill. There is no application-related intent, no ATS/company-name signal, and no tracker-update purpose -- general inbox triage is out of scope for a skill whose entire purpose is syncing the job tracker from application-related mail.

evals.prompt: Email the Acme recruiter and ask for an update on where my application stands.
evals.expected_behavior: Does not invoke email-sync, or if it does surface as related, refuses to send. This skill is read-only on the mailbox and never sends, replies, archives, deletes, or labels, even on an explicit user request to send -- composing and sending mail is out of scope for a scan-and-classify skill.

evals.prompt: I never heard anything back from Acme after three weeks -- just go ahead and mark that one rejected in the tracker.
evals.expected_behavior: Judgment call. The request asks for a status change based on silence/inference rather than a request to check email. The skill's core invariant is that it never invents statuses -- if it engages at all, the right move is to actually scan the mailbox for real evidence of a rejection (or confirm none exists) rather than writing status=rejected on the user's assumption alone; three weeks of silence is not itself a classify-table signal. A direct manual override of the tracker without any evidence check would violate the 'update from real evidence, never invent' invariant.
